what_was_built.store: kb.catalog.storage.LocalBlobStore — content-addressed, append-only, fsync + atomic rename + directory fsync, staging area inside the store root so os.replace never degrades to a copy. A key is validated against the same regex as the manifest CHECK and resolved inside the root, so containment is a property of the join rather than of the string.
what_was_built.object_key: blobs/<library-hex>/<aa>/<bb>/<sha256>. Immutable, derived from the digest, never a mutable path. The library scope is deliberate and is explained in findings_for_the_next_owner.
what_was_built.routes: POST /libraries/{id}/sources/upload (multipart), POST /libraries/{id}/sources/from-url (JSON), GET /sources/{id}/original (whole body or a single byte Range).
what_was_built.schema: kb.storage_backend (routing registry, seeded with the 'local' adapter), kb.object_manifest (the only path from an object key to a readable source, FK to kb.source(object_key)), kb.ingest (one submission attempt, UNIQUE (library_id, idempotency_key)).
what_was_built.url_ingestion: http/https only; no credentials in the URL; no numeric address forms; every resolved address checked; IP literals checked without consulting a resolver; every redirect hop re-validated from scratch; hops capped at 5; the address actually connected to compared with the approved set.
what_was_built.deduplication: scoped to the library. A re-upload of identical bytes resolves to the source that already holds them, with no second source row and no second manifest. A reply never mentions any other library.
what_was_built.data_boundary: kb.catalog.upload_data — the upload path is structurally inert (no eval/exec/compile/subprocess/pickle/import anywhere in the five card modules, proved over the parsed AST with aliases resolved), plus an explicit unbreakable fence for the point where source text is later placed in front of something that interprets text, plus a bounded directive scanner that reports to the review queue and never acts.

central_invariant.mutation_tested: eleven mutations were injected and reverted; each was rejected by at least one test. (1) follow_redirects=True failed 6 SSRF tests including every redirect re-validation case. (2) is_blocked_address returning False failed the IPv4-mapped-loopback case. (3) dedup scoped across all libraries instead of one failed test_the_same_bytes_in_two_libraries_are_two_sources and test_a_dedup_answer_never_names_another_library. (4) the manifest INSERT without the hash comparison failed 19 tests. (5) removing _require_contributor failed test_a_reader_may_not_upload. (6) fabricating a retrieval time for a file upload failed test_a_file_upload_records_no_url_and_no_retrieval_time. (7) removing the cross-submitter idempotency refusal failed test_an_idempotency_key_belonging_to_another_submitter_is_refused. (8) an aliased os.system failed the AST test — the first version of that test used a textual match and a bare 'compile(' check, and both defects were found this way and fixed. (9) a subprocess import failed the AST test. (10) not deleting the staging temp file on failure failed 3 tests. (11) replacing the JOIN to kb.object_manifest with a LEFT JOIN failed test_a_source_whose_manifest_was_removed_is_not_downloadable. Two further mutations were tried and did NOT fail anything: deleting the explicit 169.254.0.0/16 entry from BLOCKED_NETWORKS (ipaddress.is_global already covers link-local, so the entry is deliberate redundancy and not load-bearing) and a no-op rewrite of read_original that I had written wrong; the honest first version of the blocklist is therefore only half-proved by mutation, and the is_global backstop is the half that is.

findings_for_the_next_owner.finding: kb.source_version has RLS enabled and forced with exactly one policy, source_version_read. There is no write policy at all, so kb_app cannot INSERT a version even though 0002 grants it INSERT on every table — 'canonical source version' was unreachable by any runtime caller. Found by running it, not by reading it: the first submission failed with 'new row violates row-level security policy for table source_version'.
findings_for_the_next_owner.action_taken: narrowly worked around in 0004 with source_version_write, an INSERT-only policy requiring contributor on the library of the source being versioned. No UPDATE and no DELETE policy was added, so a version stays as immutable as 0001 intended. The single-owner fix is the same policy in 0002, or moving it wherever kb.source_version's policies end up living.

findings_for_the_next_owner.finding: kb.source.object_key is UNIQUE across the whole installation. That makes a globally content-only key impossible to reuse: the same book submitted to a second library could not become a second source at all, and the only answers left would be a refusal that says 'this file already exists' — the exact A20 disclosure ACCESS-MODEL forbids — or a per-library scope. C10 chose the scope and paid for it: identical bytes submitted to two libraries are stored twice.
findings_for_the_next_owner.action_taken: object keys are blobs/<library-hex>/<aa>/<bb>/<sha256>. Deduplication still works exactly where it is allowed to, inside one library. The contract change this card proposes, for the single DDL owner, is to relax the constraint to UNIQUE (library_id, object_key) — which would make the key purely content-derived again and remove the duplication. Not applied here: 0001 is outside this card's allowed paths.

findings_for_the_next_owner.finding: A URL naming an IP literal is refused on the address in the URL and is never handed to a resolver. This is not decoration: a resolver that mapped 169.254.169.254 to a public address would turn the metadata-endpoint block into a suggestion, and the mock-resolver test proves the resolver is not called for a literal. The related bypasses that are also closed are the decimal (2130706433), hexadecimal (0x7f000001) and octal-padded (0177.0.0.1) forms, which ipaddress rejects and getaddrinfo may or may not expand.
findings_for_the_next_owner.action_taken: implemented and tested: test_the_ip_literal_is_refused_without_consulting_a_resolver and three cases of test_a_url_that_is_not_plain_public_http_is_refused

findings_for_the_next_owner.finding: A rejected submission that dies mid-write leaves an object on the volume with no manifest. That is by design — it is the residue on the safe side of the invariant and nothing can reach it — but it is unreferenced bytes, and nothing in this card garbage-collects them. A process that dies between 'bytes stored' and 'source committed', repeatedly with the same content, stores that content once; with different content, once per attempt.
findings_for_the_next_owner.action_taken: documented, not solved. The fix is a sweeper that lists objects with no manifest older than some age, and it belongs with the operations card rather than here; the card's acceptance list does not ask for it. test_bytes_on_the_volume_without_a_manifest_are_unreachable proves the residue is inert in the meantime.

findings_for_the_next_owner.finding: The peer-address check (defence against DNS rebinding) reads httpx's network_stream extension, which is present for a real TCP transport and absent for a mock one. It is therefore a strengthening check that the unit tests exercise through a stand-in, and it is genuinely exercised against real sockets only on the refusal path — a refused URL never reaches a response, so no successful fetch in this environment exercised it against a live peer.
findings_for_the_next_owner.action_taken: tested directly (_verify_peer over a Response carrying a stand-in network_stream) and its absence from the mock path is stated in the module docstring rather than glossed.

findings_for_the_next_owner.finding: The URL route reads app.state.source_transport and app.state.source_resolver. They are process configuration, unset in production, and nothing in a request maps to them — but they are a seam, and a seam is a place a future change could widen.
findings_for_the_next_owner.action_taken: documented at the top of the module and at the point of use; the real production path is the one test_a_refused_url_is_a_400_and_leaves_no_row exercises, with no transport configured at all
